title: Choose Ganga Vedha's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Gear Room. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Gear Room
options.lineage: river-safety gear: stencilled helmets, PFD webbing, riveted spec plates, laminated limit tags
options.thesis: Rishikesh sold by the kilometre, with every limit printed on the tag — the operator that shows you the numbers instead of the drone footage.
options.viewport: Orange webbing status strap pinned across the top carrying today's river reading. Below it, a hard split: left, KM-scale headline in expanded grotesque on wet-slate ground with the enquiry action directly beneath; right, one hard-cropped photograph with a riveted spec plate clamped over its bottom edge. The three service plates break the fold.
options.risk: Industrial can read cold or construction-site if the photography is weak — and there are no real photos yet. The type, colour fields and plates carry it alone, but the ceiling rises sharply once the client supplies images.

raised.raise: Availability is now the loudest state in the system, not a badge — a running stretch is lit in full orange, a closed one drains to slate and takes the stamp.
Grade owns a colour by law — green, blue, orange — never decoration, and every plate snaps to a hard module with nothing off-grid.
Preview before commit: the enquiry stamps a full quote before submit is possible, and the admin closure control previews exactly what visitors will see.
Scale is mapped to decision weight — the kilometre numeral and the price are the largest things on a card, not uniform template slots.
River status is one dominant global field governing the whole site's state, and the status strap is the single element that never scrolls away.

options.label: The River Chart
options.thesis: The whole site drawn as a guide's river map: one blue line down the page, kilometres measured along it, rapids as named ticks.
options.viewport: The river line enters top-left and runs full height. The headline sits in the margin as a cartographer's note. The three services are three annotated nodes on the line, kilometres ticking between them.
options.risk: This is the obvious answer. Map-as-navigation for a river product is where most runs land, and chart-cream plus ink plus one vermilion sits inside a known generated-interface cluster. It will be lovely and it will not surprise anyone.
options.case: Topped my grounded list on resonance: it makes the kilometre mechanism literal and beautiful. Shown so the familiarity trade is yours to make, not mine.

options.label: Punched Brocade
options.lineage: jacquard loom brocade woven from punch-card instructions
options.thesis: Each rafting stretch is a woven row; the kilometre sequence is the punch pattern, traceable from motif to row to single thread.
options.viewport: Banded rows down the page, one stretch per row, ledger digits carrying km, duration and price in strict columns, gold motif resolving across the band.
options.risk: Reads as a wedding venue rather than a river operator, and gold-on-midnight fights daylight water photography.
options.case: Holds product clarity outright — the row-banded ledger is a genuinely better grammar for comparing five stretches by number than anything else dealt, and its motif-row-card traceability maps cleanly onto service-stretch-rapid. Loses audience identification: a 25-year-old comparing operators on a phone does not identify with brocade.

options.label: Arcade Marquee Row
options.lineage: backlit arcade marquees down a dark aisle
options.thesis: Three services as three lit marquees, attract screens previewing before you commit a coin.
options.viewport: One cabinet per destination down a dark aisle, the glowing marquee band as signpost.
options.risk: Undercuts the safety trust this product must earn, and a dark aisle hides the prices people came to compare.
options.case: Loses both axes: rafting buyers do not live in arcades, and coin-in maps onto nothing in an enquiry flow.
options.kept: Lit-state as primary wayfinding — one destination unmistakably on at a time.

options.label: CRT Arcade Pixel Glow
options.thesis: A sixteen-colour palette law where every state is a sprite swap and nothing sits off-grid.
options.viewport: Tile-grid playfield with eight-by-eight caps pinned to the top edge.
options.risk: Pixel art cannot show real Himalayan water, which this product must show.
options.case: Loses both axes on fusion: the grid discipline is real, but sprite rendering is in direct conflict with the photography the product depends on.
options.kept: Palette as law — grade colours encode meaning, never decorate — and a hard module with nothing off-grid.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight Bay
options.lineage: amber-lit printing darkrooms with timed baths
options.thesis: Booking staged as an irreversible chemical process through fixed stations.
options.viewport: Fixed stations in order — compose, expose, develop, fix, wash — linearising on phones.
options.risk: Amber monochrome drains the river imagery the product is selling.
options.case: Loses both axes: the staged flow is elegant but travellers do not identify with darkroom craft, and a monochrome wash defeats the photography.
options.kept: Test-strip discipline — preview the result before the action commits.

options.label: Variety Telop Field
options.thesis: Outlined captions placed free in the frame, scaled to the emotion of the moment.
options.viewport: Captions landing free across the frame, rotation as punctuation, no fixed band.
options.risk: Free placement destroys the price and kilometre scanability the whole product rests on.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is a Japanese broadcast grammar with no purchase on an Indian adventure audience, and unfixed placement is fatal to comparison.
options.kept: Scale mapped to intensity — hierarchy driven by meaning rather than by slot.

options.label: Gravity-Rain Garden
options.lineage: surreal gardens where rain falls by the colour of its cloud
options.thesis: One dominant field governs everything; only the legend is held level.
options.viewport: A garden of local gravities, labels falling toward their clouds, the legend the only level thing.
options.risk: Dreamlike surrealism reads as unserious for an operator whose core promise is safety.
options.case: Loses both axes: the monsoon rhyme is tempting, but bent baselines wreck price scanning and the register contradicts the trust this surface must build.
options.kept: One dominant global field the whole surface obeys, with the legend fixed and never moving.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What every Rishikesh operator ships, executed at the craft level of the best of them.
canonCard.viewport: Whitewater hero video under a dark gradient, white bold headline, orange rounded CTA, three glass cards with rating chips, trust badges, testimonial carousel, sticky WhatsApp bubble.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from DroneCraft and every competitor by design — which is also exactly what the client pointed at.
